subtle.$description: subtle interactive fill — one step darker than surface (hover rows, selection, hover chips); mirrors --color-text-subtle (#174)

elevated.$description: white — floats above surface (gray-100) via shadow

forward.$description: Intent surfaces (#318). Use these to rank surfaces by temperature: forward for the one thing a screen should lead with, recede for chrome that should step back. They change temperature, not lightness, so contrast barely moves. Ranking by temperature is a tertiary affordance: it guides the eye but never carries meaning on its own, since a deltaE 5 to 15 shift is lost on a washed-out screen or to a reader who cannot tell the hues apart. — same lightness as the page, warm

recede.$description: same lightness as bg-surface, cool; use text-subtle-on-surface on it

muted.$description: Neutral fill that reads on page, surface and elevated alike, which bg-subtle cannot (deltaE 3 from surface in light). deltaE 13 / 8 / 14 from page / surface / elevated. Used at rest by the default badge (#321) and on hover by bg-hover (#322). — text-default OKCA 6.5 on this bg ✅

hover.$description: Hover fill for transparent controls: ghost buttons and close/dismiss actions (#322).

code.$description: A teal tint, deltaE 9 from the page in light and 8 in dark, replacing the filled navy-800 panel (deltaE 79 from white), which was hard to read at length. Teal at hue 195 is clear of every brand and status hue in both modes (#318); the burgundy tint it replaced sat deltaE 5.6 from error-bg. Text is the ordinary body colour, so the pair needs no inverse. — text-default OKCA 9.6 on this bg ✅

subtle.$description: OKCA 4.8 on page ✅ — gray-500 (L=0.56) was OKCA 3.8; stepped to L=0.50 for OKCA compliance (#14)

subtle-on-surface.$description: OKCA 5.0 on bg-surface ✅ — gray-600 (L=0.46) was OKCA 4.5 on gray-100; stepped to L=0.44 (#14)

subtle-on-inverse.$description: OKCA 7.6 on bg-inverse ✅ — muted links on dark nav/tabs

message.$description: Component-scoped: toast message text. Every toast sits on bg-surface since #292. — OKCA 9.3 on bg-surface ✅

strong.$description: Separator/divider fill — decorative, carries no 1.4.11 floor: OKCA 1.3 on page. Do not reach for it as a control boundary; that is border-control. candor-slider used it for the unfilled half of its track, the one place the figure was load-bearing; since #247 the slider rail is border-control.

on-inverse.$description: subtle divider on navy-800 inverse surface

control.$description: Form control boundaries must meet WCAG 1.4.11 non-text contrast (3:1 OKCA), and must meet it on *every* background a control can sit on — not just the page. L=0.53 is the lightest value that clears 3.0 against the worst of them; it sits on gray-600 (L=0.50), the nearest ramp step on the safe side (#318): OKCA 4.8 on page ✅, OKCA 3.8 on bg-surface ✅.  This used to be gray-500 (L=0.56) with a --color-border-control-on-surface sibling the consumer applied by hand on surface containers. That token is gone (5.0.0). It was a correctness property delegated to whoever remembered the rule, and the repo itself remembered it once out of twice — the colour-iterator example shipped six controls whose boundary was OKCA 2.8 on bg-surface, and the switch's off-state thumb sits on a track that carries its own bg-surface fill, so that one was below the floor in every consumer regardless of what the page behind it was doing (#217). One value that is safe everywhere removes the failure mode instead of documenting it; it lands deltaE 3 from the old base and deltaE 3 from the sibling it replaces, i.e. imperceptibly between the two colours it supersedes.

code.$description: deliberate: the tint separates the block from the page on its own; dark mode adds a rule (#242)

thumb.$description: Form-control knob fill (slider/switch thumb) — a light puck; pairs with --color-border-control (darker) for the edge. icon/border use (non-text UI). — white knob in light — icon/border use

destructive.$description: Takes the error red. It was a boosted burgundy (H=347), kept apart from error on the reasoning that destructive is a chosen action, not a failure. That put it deltaE 8 from --color-action-secondary, the burgundy that fills badges, chips and the current nav item, so a "Featured" badge matched the delete button. Error and destructive both mean "take care", so sharing red misleads no one; deltaE to secondary is now 24 light / 17 dark (#318). Both modes: outlined — transparent bg, red border+text.

destructive-text.$description: outlined, so page and bg-surface are both real placements (#224); figures on the pairings

destructive-border.$description: matches text — no separate pairing: identical value, and a border's 3.0 non-text floor is strictly below the text floor already measured

tertiary.$description: No border — structural identity is the fill (distinct from secondary's outline). — was gray-100; bumped for visibility without border

link.$description: azure-400 is the brand original (#1493FB) — use on dark backgrounds only. azure-500/600 are the accessible steps for use on white backgrounds. — OKCA 5.3 on white ✅ — azure-500 (L=0.53) was OKCA 4.4; stepped to L=0.49 for OKCA compliance (#14)

link-visited.$description: OKCA 5.8 on white ✅ — honors universal :visited convention

error.$description: Base colors: non-text use only (icons, borders, indicators). For text on light status-bg, use --color-status-*-text (contrast-validated below). — icon/border use — OKCA 3.6 on error-bg ✅ (WCAG 1.4.11)

error-bg.$description: at the sRGB chroma ceiling for this L and H (0.03 is out of gamut), so it cannot get redder without getting darker. deltaE 14 from warning-bg since warning moved to gold (it was 4 against amber), but a pale tint is still not a variant channel (#214, #242, #318)

error-text.$description: OKCA 5.4 on error-bg ✅ — C=0.22 exceeded what sRGB holds at this L and H, so the token specified no single colour and its recorded 4.6 was undefined; re-authored to the boundary, same L and H (#225)

success-bg.$description: green and gold have more chroma room at L 0.95 than red, which is why error alone sits at 0.02 (#242)

success-text.$description: OKCA 5.1 on success-bg ✅ — L=0.50 was OKCA 4.2; stepped to L=0.46 (#14)

warning.$description: gold since #318; OKCA 3.1 on bg-surface ✅, the lightest gold that clears the non-text floor there — icon/border use — OKCA 3.5 on warning-bg ✅ (WCAG 1.4.11)

warning-bg.$description: gold has chroma room at L 0.95 that amber did not (amber topped out at 0.02), so this tint is deltaE 14 from error-bg; still not a variant channel (#214, #242, #318)

warning-text.$description: OKCA 6.2 on warning-bg ✅ — gold since #318 (was amber, H=53.54). Reads olive-brown at this lightness: yellow loses the most chroma as it darkens, and the text has to be this dark to clear its floor on bg-surface

text.$description: A book indent, set a step larger in italic, on the page itself. No wash and no side bar: that pairing reads as machine-made (#292). — OKCA 11.9 on page ✅

bg.$description: A neutral panel. The indigo wash and left bar went in #292. — text-default OKCA 9.3 on this bg ✅

subtle.$description: subtle interactive fill — a hair lighter than surface in dark (direction flips vs light) (#174). Cooled counterpart of gray-700 so it recedes on the cool-navy surfaces instead of advancing (warm advances / cool recedes); L preserved.

elevated.$description: one step above surface; shares gray-cool-800 with bg-subtle

forward.$description: Intent surfaces (#318). Dark surfaces are already cool, so recede steps down toward the page; forward keeps the card lightness and turns warm.

muted.$description: gray-cool-700: deltaE 18 / 13 / 8 from page / surface / elevated, and dark enough that text-default keeps 4.5 (gray-cool-600 gives 4.3) (#321, #322). — text-default OKCA 5.7 on this bg ✅

code.$description: Teal tint, deltaE 8 from the cool page: the hue change carries the separation, so the block stays nearly as dark as the page. Border still required, since lightness alone barely differs at these low L values. — text-default OKCA 11.4 on this bg ✅ — code text inherits it

default.$description: OKCA 12.9 on bg-page ✅ — off-white with cool undertone; white OKCA 19.2 on bg-page is harsh

disabled.$description: OKCA 2.0 on bg-page — intentionally below AA (1.4.3-exempt; see #134)

subtle-on-inverse.$description: muted text on white inverse surface

on-action.$description: OKCA 11.2 on action-primary ✅ — same as bg-page; was OKCA 7.0 on the sky-blue primary (#318); gray-800 (L=0.24) was OKCA 5.6, fails 14px bold threshold of 6.5

message.$description: Component-scoped: toast message text. Every toast sits on bg-surface since #292, where the three status backgrounds used to be. — OKCA 5.6 on bg-surface ✅ — intentionally subtle in dark mode; dimming is a feature, not a bug

strong.$description: OKCA 3.5 on bg-page. Reads as a 1.4.11 pass and is one, but do not read it as a property of the token: the light value of the same token clears barely a third of that against its own page, and it is the same separator in both modes. The token is decorative; dark simply clears a bar the light mode misses, which is a fact about two greys and not a guarantee (#247).

on-inverse.$description: subtle divider on white inverse surface

control.$description: Dark needs its own value: contrast here means a *lighter* edge, so the light mode's L=0.53 would move the wrong way against a dark surface. The worst dark background is bg-elevated, which is lighter than surface. It holds every option panel, the drawer, the modal and the chat input, so form-control borders and scrollbar thumbs both sit on it. L=0.58 was chosen against page and surface only and measured 2.6 there, with no pairing to say so (#307). L=0.62 clears it with 0.1 of margin: L=0.61 sits exactly on 3.0, so any later change to bg-elevated would push it under: OKCA 3.1 on dark bg-elevated ✅, OKCA 3.9 on dark bg-surface ✅, OKCA 4.6 on dark page ✅. Replaces the dark --color-border-control-on-surface (L=0.60) — see the light-mode note above for why the sibling is gone.

thumb.$description: Light puck on the dark track — fill stays light (border-control 0.62 is the darker edge). icon/border use (non-text UI). — oklch(0.91) light knob in dark — icon/border use

primary.$description: A pale navy from the brand ramp, so dark mode reads as the same navy as light. It was a boosted sky blue, oklch(0.79 0.11 245), deltaE 3 from --color-link (2 between their hovers), so a primary button and a link beside it were the same colour. navy-200 is deltaE 14 from the link and 6 from its hover, and a quiet fill lets the content around it lead (#318). Deliberately no figures here. Both that this comment used to carry were duplicates recorded better elsewhere, and one had gone stale unnoticed because the export discarded this comment entirely (#224): it credited the label as gray-800, which was OKCA 5.6 here, but the label stopped being gray-800 when --color-text-on-action moved to the bg-page navy for exactly that reason — it fails the 14px bold floor of 6.5. That token's own comment records the change and is audited; this one restated it and rotted. — OKCA 11.7 on bg-page ✅

secondary.$description: Label on the secondary fill: bg-page OKCA 7.3 on this bg ✅ — OKCA 7.6 on bg-page ✅ (fill vs page)

destructive.$description: Outlined — same pattern as light mode, and the same error red (#318).

destructive-text.$description: Was oklch(0.78 0.15 347), stepped from L=0.75 so the label cleared its floor on bg-surface as well as the page — a delete confirmation usually sits in a modal or card (#224). The error red clears both with more margin; figures on the pairings.

destructive-border.$description: matches text — no separate pairing: identical value, and a border's 3.0 non-text floor is strictly below the text floor already measured

tertiary.$description: ⚠️  fill is only OKCA 1.1 on page — intentionally subtle in dark mode. Text (gray-0) on tertiary bg remains readable. Uses the cool-gray ramp (matching bg-subtle) so tertiary recedes on the cool-navy surfaces instead of advancing and competing with the primary button (warm advances / cool recedes); L preserved, so white OKCA 13.0 on this bg ✅. Revisit if buttons need more prominence in dark.

error.$description: Lightened foreground colors to meet contrast on dark backgrounds. Backgrounds mirror light-mode approach: near-neutral dark surface (C≈0.02), letting the border/icon carry the full color signal. High-chroma fills were competing with vivid borders and creating a "glowing" effect. — icon/border use — not required to pass text contrast

error-text.$description: OKCA 6.0 on error-bg ✅ — C=0.22 was far outside sRGB, so the token named no single colour and every figure recorded for it was undefined; its nearest in-gamut form was OKCA 3.4, which is how five failures sat inside a passing audit (#222). Re-authored to the boundary, same L and H (#225). L=0.77 was OKCA 4.2; stepped to L=0.79 (#14) — a step taken against the unrenderable value, kept because it still holds for the renderable one

success.$description: icon/border use — not required to pass text contrast

warning.$description: icon/border use — not required to pass text contrast

warning-text.$description: OKCA 7.1 on warning-bg ✅ — gold since #318 (was amber, H=53.54)

text.$description: A book indent, set a step larger in italic, on the page itself. No wash and no side bar: that pairing reads as machine-made (#292). — OKCA 11.9 on page ✅

bg.$description: A neutral panel. The indigo wash and left bar went in #292. — text-default OKCA 9.3 on this bg ✅
